subject: geography
title: Case Study: Japan and Haiti
welcome_lead: Two earthquakes, two very different outcomes. Compare Japan 2011 and Haiti 2010 to see why preparation matters.
meta_desc: KS3 Geography case study comparing Japan 2011 and Haiti 2010 earthquakes.
final_note: Well done! You can now compare impacts in rich and poor countries.

concepts.def: Giant sea wave caused by undersea earthquake.
Size or strength of an earthquake.
Higher Income Country, wealthy and developed.
Lower Income Country, poorer and less developed.
Later impacts like disease or homelessness.

walkthroughs.body_html: A magnitude 9.0 quake struck off Japan's coast, triggering a deadly tsunami. Japan's strict building codes saved many lives, but the tsunami killed around 15,000 people.
Haiti's quake measured 7.0 — smaller than Japan's — but killed over 200,000 people. Weak buildings and poor emergency services made things worse.
HICs like Japan can afford earthquake-proof buildings, drills and warnings. LICs like Haiti often cannot, so people suffer more.
